rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.

evidence_decisions.note: New paper evaluations use supported fresh evidence. CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes
Spread/total splits need exact source-line identity and remain display-only
Missing evidence retains the original forecast and is explicitly recorded
Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

cfb_efficiency.note: Offensive EPA: higher is better. Defensive EPA allowed: lower is better; negative is favorable. These are equal-game averages of non-garbage-time EPA/play, not opponent-adjusted ratings. The existing CFB spread forecast already uses opponent-adjusted EPA alongside other metrics; do not add these descriptive averages to its probability again. Passing/rushing are context, not a separately validated matchup edge. Missing values mean unknown. Check sample, opponent strength, injuries and pace; EPA alone is not a spread, total, player projection or bet instruction. Source: local ESPN-derived EPA, not CFBD PPA; provider values are not interchangeable.

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. All four overall samples need at least four games and fresh, matched CFBD evidence. Totals, underdog spreads, missing/stale samples and mixed evidence retain existing rules. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: 1) Possible double-adjustment: sportsbook.py:190-196 applies Context.game() and ranks options by adjusted probability, but original_q (line 196) picks the best unadjusted edge, so selection_changed compares different objectives; evidence_decisions.py:97 finish() then applies outcome_retraining after evidence blends, and the stake cap/affects_betting flag (lines 100-103) treats retraining and evidence changes identically, obscuring attribution. In sportsbook.py:205 the stake cap only tightens, fine, but line 206 status uses edge from the adjusted probability against a threshold that may already include retraining shifts. Needs human validation. 2) Temporal/identity hygiene is mostly sound (quotes filtered observed/updated < tip and <= now at sportsbook.py:99; trend rows require date < today at evidence_decisions.py:153), but evidence_decisions.py:56 filters splits with tip_utc>now yet matching uses a 1200s tip window and fuzzy mascot-suffix team matching (lines 182-187), a misidentification hypothesis for similarly named teams. Injury freshness check at line 127 passes only if `latest` is non-empty, so missing latest availability silently invalidates; OK but availability_id tied to a single fetched_utc stamp (line 63-64) could drop all injury data if stamps differ. 3) Accounting/settlement: sportsbook.py:201 uses ticket cash/exposure computed from open_rows inside the loop, but cash is read before insertion each iteration so it updates correctly; grade() at line 143 treats push-eligible three-way soccer as win/loss only (no push), fine. Settlement only requires completed flag and non-negative integer scores; no verification of final status or period (e.g. OT/regulation for soccer). Missing validation: saved tests refer to a different source snapshot, so no test evidence certifies this code; calibration is explicitly uncalibrated (normal-error sigma assumptions, sportsbook.py:125).

Top observations (static review, not executed): (1) news_hypotheses.py line 88-92 plus 102/105: team is inferred from the player's last history row and then matched to the quote's player_team abbreviation, but the teammate-minutes sample at line 49 uses only games since the teammate first appeared with this team, and line 102 uses the injured player's last 10 minutes as a ranking proxy; if history is stale or a trade occurred, identity checks rest on stale team data (hypothesis, needs validation). Also line 94 treats any non-active/available/probable own status as a hold but a player missing from the injury file is assumed healthy, which is unverified. (2) news_hypotheses.py lines 52-56: the revision mixes a 30-game recency-weighted baseline minutes with a with/without mean split drawn from the full pooled sample, and 'missing' games include non-injury absences (DNP-coach, suspension, rest); shrinkage n/(n+10) is ad hoc and uncalibrated. SHADOW_CANDIDATE threshold edge>=.02 at line 117 compares model probability to raw implied probability 1/decimal(price) with no vig removal, which inflates apparent edge; best-of-books selection at line 110 (max edge over quotes) is a selection-bias/winner's-curse optimistic gap, and the Brier comparison at 130-131 scores only the selected quote. Calibration is unvalidated. (3) context_trends.py lines 28-34: quote selection filters to the chosen book and requires obs within 90 minutes of tip, which is leakage-safe, but line 85 picks book via min(options by book name), arbitrary rather than best/consistent; line 13 uses game_date < today but line 23 requires tip<now, fine. Minor: line 94-95 dedupes the identity digest in a loop but a duplicate check at 98-99 is redundant, and exception handling at 67 swallows only OSError/ValueError/KeyError so other parse errors crash the tick. Tests are stale for this snapshot; rerun before approval.

Top observations (review-only; no code run; saved tests belong to a different source snapshot, so no test evidence applies). 1) Definite accounting/identity concern, sportsbook.py:194-206: selection picks max(edge-threshold) across books/sides, but 'edge' for CFB/injury paths is computed from d['probability'], while the stake formula at line 201 and the pass/accept test at 206 compare edge to decision['threshold'] of the chosen quote only; a blocked quote can still be selected when no eligible option exists (eligible or options) and is then marked 'pass' correctly, but 'changed' (line 197) compares against original_q chosen by raw edge, so selection_changed can be reported true purely from tie-breaking on book name. 2) Temporal/staleness: evidence_decisions.py:54 filters splits by captured_utc freshness (<=0.5h) but allows captured_utc in the future relative to now (fresh() permits only past via timedelta(0)<=...; splits path uses the same fn, OK), whereas evidence_decisions.py:31-34 reads rows keyed on created_utc but never checks the news/trend game tip vs now; and line 122 'last_history_date < now.date()' uses UTC date, which can admit same-local-day history. Context.signature (line 71-73) includes self.ai dicts directly, so any AI text change re-triggers fresh decisions each tick: unbounded sb_decisions growth is plausible (hypothesis, not verified). 3) Calibration/double-adjustment: sportsbook.py:132 adds a fixed bias to probabilities, then evidence blends (evidence_decisions.py:133) off the already-biased prior; the 5pp cap and fixed weights (lines 11-12) are explicitly uncalibrated, and normal-error sigma values (sportsbook.py:125) are assumptions, so reported 'edge' is not a validated advantage. Also grade() pushes on quarter-lines are filtered at load (line 58) but Asian-handicap quotes via site_odds/mlb loaders bypass that filter (line 70-76), a possible settlement error.
